A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same sharpness-based analysis of diffusion-model memorization and the SAIL mitigation method. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–E support a reliable comparison despite the title and layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on a two-dimensional Gaussian mixture, MNIST, and Stable Diffusion, including detection results in Table 1 and mitigation results in Figure 6 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and additionally reports an unsuccessful alternative mitigation objective in Appendix D.2.

M1.justification: The Hessian-weighted detection metric, SAIL objective, finite-difference approximation, Gaussian regularization, and initialization-optimization procedure remain unchanged. The alternative objective discussed in v3 is an unsuccessful experimental control.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Gaussian-mixture and MNIST experiments, Stable Diffusion v1.4/v2.0, and memorized and non-memorized prompt sources. Appendices C–D introduce no additional dataset, population, or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 6 retain their comparator sets. Appendix D.2 newly reports a qualitative comparison with an initial-noise optimization variant using Wen’s squared score-difference objective in place of SAIL’s sharpness term.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 adds an objective-replacement control assessed through convergence. Existing benchmark sample counts, DDIM schedules, metrics, and hyperparameter grids remain unchanged; further evaluation settings for the added control are not supplied.

E4.justification: v3 adds a component ablation asking whether Wen’s metric can replace SAIL’s first loss term, reporting failure to converge. The existing curvature analyses, parameter sweeps, and qualitative examples are retained.

E5.justification: Generation averaging in Table 1, five generations per prompt for mitigation, and Figure 3’s percentile bands remain unchanged. The added convergence finding supplies no new run counts, seed information, or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Appendix D.2 adds the qualitative finding that the replacement objective fails to converge. Table 1’s scores are identical, and existing plotted trends remain unchanged. Figure 3 corrects missing negative tick-label signs without changing those trends.

T1.justification: v2 establishes Lemma 4.1 for Gaussian distributions. v3 adds Appendix B.2, generalizing the expected score-norm/Hessian-trace identity under finite-score and boundary conditions, with an integration-by-parts proof. Other lemmas and Appendix A’s derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: sharpness-based analysis, justification of Wen’s metric, early detection, and SAIL mitigation. The title’s added emphasis on mitigation describes a contribution already present in v2.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly explains the identity’s non-Gaussian applicability while retaining a Gaussian focus for analysis. Appendix D.2 tentatively attributes the alternative objective’s failure to its weaker sensitivity during early generation, adding a rationale for the retained objective.

D1.justification: The pseudocode, training-loss details, optimizer settings, SAIL regularization values, stopping-threshold grids, and prompt-selection details remain unchanged. The added control provides no additional implementation settings or resource-access information.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Achilli et al. (2024) and Hyvärinen (2005), removes Stein et al. (2023), and refines Section 2’s distinction between aggregated sharpness statistics and analyses of individual feature components.

P1.justification: The title, author information, and selected introduction, related-work, Gaussian-explanation, and conclusion passages are edited. Acknowledgement and Impact Statement sections are added. The principal section order and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column formatting, extensively reflowing text, equations, figures, and captions. Figure 3 is re-exported with missing negative tick signs restored. The appendix’s qualitative figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: v3 improves theoretical clarity through the non-Gaussian identity and proof, corrects misleading axis labels in Figure 3, and documents an unsuccessful alternative objective. These are useful but limited gains: the convergence finding lacks quantitative evidence and detailed settings, while the principal method and experimental results remain unchanged.
